newsitem.title: USA: America Online shuts access points in Russia.
newsitem.headline: America Online shuts access points in Russia.

text.p: America Online Inc. said Wednesday it shut down its access phone numbers for customers in Russia because of fraudulent credit card use and other reasons it is still investigating.

While AOL does not provide a localised AOL service for Russia, it has many local phone numbers for its mobile users visiting Russia or for Russian computer users to access AOL via local numbers in Russia.

"There was an unusual surge of activity and a rise in the number of hours (online) coming through those access numbers," said Tatiana Gau, vice president for integrity assurance at Dulles, Va.-based AOL.
AOL estimates that anywhere from several hundred to several thousand users will be affected by the shutdown of the access phone numbers.

Gau said that when AOL started to look at the activity in the accounts of those logging onto the service from Russia, a number of accounts were fraudulently registered, using stolen credit card numbers. She did not give any indication of when the access numbers would be reinstated.
"We shut down the access points so we can get a better idea of what was going on," Gau said. "We don't have the full data."
Fraudulent registration was only one example of illicit activity, she said.
Credit card fraud is a growing problem in Russia, where organised crime has become a powerful force in business, according to local press reports.
